question: A 54-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of episodic palpitations for the past 12 hours. He has no chest pain. He has coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His current medications include aspirin, insulin, and atorvastatin. His pulse is 155/min and blood pressure is 116/77 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. An ECG shows monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. An amiodarone bolus and infusion is given, and the ventricular tachycardia converts to normal sinus rhythm. He is discharged home with oral amiodarone. Which of the following is the most likely adverse effect associated with long-term use of this medication?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Amiodarone" -> "antiarrhythmic medication" -> "used to treat ventricular tachycardia" -> "converted VT to normal sinus rhythm" -> "long-term use" -> "associated with potential adverse effects" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Amiodarone" -> "long-term use" -> "known to cause pulmonary toxicity" -> "chronic interstitial pneumonitis" -> "possible adverse effect" -> 70%
analysis: Amiodarone is known to be associated with chronic interstitial pneumonitis as a potential adverse effect with long-term use. This condition can present with symptoms such as dyspnea, cough, and fever.
